points: The next earnings print will reveal whether Roku's Q2 platform revenue strength reflects durable ad demand or one-time factors, and management's Q3 guidance will show if that momentum can carry through the back half of 2026.

With advertising revenue already at $2.33B and growing 13%, connected-TV ad budgets could keep shifting to Roku in the quarters ahead, lifting platform revenue above the FY25 18% growth pace and helping margins expand.

New content partnerships and subscription services could start adding incremental platform revenue in Q4 2026 and into 2027, making Roku less reliant on device sales and deepening its competitive moat.

The Fox $22B acquisition agreement and CEO succession plan could be resolved by year-end; if the deal closes or is clearly abandoned, the stock can re-rate on fundamentals rather than takeover speculation.
A COPPA settlement or regulatory fine that stays well below the $200M falsifier threshold could remove a major overhang in the next 6-12 months, while a larger verdict would break the long thesis.
Garmin's Oct. 28 consumer electronics report may offer an early read on holiday demand and ad spending heading into Q4 2026, which matters for Roku's device and platform revenue setup.
If streaming household growth and device adoption stay healthy, Roku can keep converting users into high-margin platform revenue through 2027, building on its first GAAP-profitable year in FY25.
